entries.name_and_variants: Cup & handle; later inverse variant separately
entries.definition: Rounded bottom between comparable rims after an advance, followed by a smaller handle. Confirm above the rim/handle resistance. Keep current bowl-fit, depth and handle gates.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `cup_handle`; bullish.

entries.definition: Repeated tests of a flat resistance level followed by a fresh qualifying close above it. Unlike a rectangle, this does not require flat support.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `horizontal_breakout`; confirmed bullish only.

entries.definition: Efficient directional impulse followed by a smaller counter-trend parallel consolidation with contracting volume. Confirm out of the flag in the pole direction.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `flag_pole`; both directions.

entries.definition: Lower swing highs and higher swing lows form converging boundaries. The completed shape is neutral; the observed breakout supplies direction.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `symmetrical_triangle`; both breakout directions.

entries.definition: Both boundaries fall and narrow; upper boundary descends faster. Bullish confirmation crosses the upper line. Label preceding decline versus a pullback within an advance separately.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `falling_wedge`; proposed context tags need new research.

entries.definition: Both boundaries rise and narrow; lower boundary rises faster. Bearish confirmation crosses the lower line. Keep context separate from shape.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `rising_wedge`; proposed context tags need new research.

entries.definition: Approximately parallel boundaries with repeated alternating touches. Separate trading a contained channel from a breakout/retest of its boundary.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `channel`; current implementation excludes confirmed breaks.

entries.definition: Flat support and falling resistance converge. Preserve the current bearish definition; an upside resolution would be a new variant, not an existing bearish success.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `descending_triangle`; downside only.

entries.definition: Three peaks, with the middle highest, following an advance. The intervening troughs form a neckline. Confirm with a close below it.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `head_shoulders`.

entries.definition: Three troughs, with the middle lowest, following a decline. Intervening peaks form the neckline. Confirm with a close above it.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Existing `inverse_head_shoulders`.

entries.definition: Flat resistance and rising support converge. Primary variant confirms above resistance; opposite-side failure/resolution is recorded separately. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/ascending-triangle).
Mirror of CH02: repeated flat support tests followed by a fresh qualifying close below support. Retain distinct support/resistance event IDs.

Repeated approximately equal highs and lows form two horizontal boundaries. Neutral while contained; confirm on a close outside. A channel with negligible slope is the same geometric family, so link aliases. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/rectangle).

A directional pole followed by a short converging consolidation; unlike a flag, boundaries are not parallel. Confirm in the pole direction. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/flag-pennant).

entries.name_and_variants: Double top; Adam/Adam, Adam/Eve, Eve/Adam, Eve/Eve
entries.definition: Two separated comparable peaks following an advance; require an intervening trough. Confirm below that trough. Adam means a sharp peak, Eve a rounded peak; these subtype classifiers need independent shape rules. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/double-top-reversal).
entries.coverage_or_priority: 1; subtype work 2

entries.name_and_variants: Double bottom; the same four shape combinations
entries.definition: Two separated comparable troughs following a decline. Confirm above the intervening peak. Reject pairs without sufficient separation or intervening recovery.
entries.coverage_or_priority: 1; subtype work 2

entries.definition: Three separated comparable peaks after an advance. Confirm below the support defined by intervening troughs. Link the earlier double-top candidate rather than rewriting its history.

Three separated comparable troughs after a decline. Confirm above intervening resistance. Earlier two-trough events retain their original timestamps. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/triple-bottom-reversal).

A sustained transition from falling to flat to rising prices, fitted as a bowl, without requiring a handle. Confirm above the prior rim resistance. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/rounding-bottom).
Proposed geometric mirror of CH19: rising to flat to falling prices. Confirm below rim support. Keep mirror assumptions explicit.
Proposed bearish mirror of CH01: rounded dome, shallow upward handle after a decline, then confirmation below support. Not a relabeling of any ordinary rounded top.

entries.name_and_variants: Broadening / megaphone; top, bottom, ascending, descending
entries.definition: Alternating swings diverge so the range expands. Tag slope and prior trend; confirm beyond the relevant outer boundary. A broadening wedge is a sloped subtype, not a converging wedge.
Broadening swings transition to contraction, with a distinct widest middle. Confirm through the final converging boundary. Prior trend and resolution determine the context label.
A full-range gap isolates one or more bars, followed by a full-range gap in the opposite direction. Confirmation exists only after the second gap; no missing-data gap may stand in for a price gap.

Proposed short, steep decline followed by rapid recovery, or its mirror; deliberately excludes a rounded bowl. Confirm only after recovery crosses a predeclared level, never at the extreme in retrospect.

Directional leg, corrective consolidation, then a second leg in the original direction. Detect at the second-leg breakout; an equal-leg projection is a reference target, not a prerequisite learned from future price. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/measured-move-bullish).

A moderate trend accelerates into a steeper extension, then breaks its prior trend support/resistance. Measure acceleration in normalized price per bar, not screen angles. The bottom version is a proposed mirror. [Reference](https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/chart-analysis/chart-patterns/bump-and-run-reversal).

KANIDA proposal: at least three successive smaller pullbacks within a base, decreasing normalized ranges and contracting volume. Confirm beyond the base boundary. This is a geometric contraction model, not a claim to reproduce a complete named discretionary trading system.
Body is at or below the configured doji threshold. Neutral shape; trade direction requires a separate rule.
Doji with at least one long shadow under the reference implementation. A stricter both-shadows definition would be a separate variant. Neutral.
Doji near the range high, negligible upper shadow and a nontrivial lower shadow. Direction depends on context and confirmation.
Doji near the range low, negligible lower shadow and a nontrivial upper shadow. Context-dependent, not automatically a short entry.
Doji near the middle of its range with long shadows on both sides. Neutral; more restrictive than generic doji.
Dragonfly-like doji with an exceptionally long lower shadow. Proposed bullish interpretation requires a preceding decline.
Small body; both shadows exceed body length. Up/down candle colors are variants of a neutral shape.
Small body and very long shadows on both sides. Neutral; library sign represents color.
Short body and short shadows. Up/down colors are descriptive; use as a shape/filter or a separately confirmed strategy.
Long body and short shadows. Up/down momentum form; classify continuation/reversal only from prior context.
Long body with both shadows negligible. Direction follows body color; the shape alone does not establish a reversal.
Long body ending near the favorable extreme: up candle closes near high, down candle near low. The opening-end shadow may remain.
Long body opens near its low for the up form or near its high for the down form. Opposite-end shadow is allowed.
Small upper-positioned body, long lower shadow, minimal upper shadow, near the previous low. Require a preceding decline for the bullish reversal study.
Small body, long lower shadow, minimal upper shadow, near the previous high. Require a preceding advance for the bearish study.
Small body with a long upper shadow and little lower shadow; reference definition also requires a downward body gap. Bullish context after a decline.
Small body, long upper shadow, little lower shadow and an upward body gap in the reference definition. Bearish context after an advance.
Second opposite-color body encloses the first body. Full-range engulfing is different. Preserve the library's edge-equality recognition grades as metadata.
Long body followed by a short body inside it. Direction is opposite the first candle; record second-candle color rather than silently requiring it to differ.
Harami whose second body is a doji. Link to the parent harami occurrence when both match.
Long down candle, then long up candle opening below the prior low and recovering beyond the first body's midpoint while remaining below its open. Bullish.
Long up candle, then down candle opening above the prior high and penetrating sufficiently into the first body without fully engulfing it. Bearish; save penetration setting.
Long body followed by a doji whose body gaps away in the first candle's direction. This is a setup, not the completed three-candle morning/evening form.
Two long opposite-color bodies finish at approximately the same close. Second candle supplies the conventional direction.
Long down body followed by a smaller down body contained within it. Bullish-context study after a decline; overlaps same-color harami geometry.
Two down candles close at approximately the same level. A close-based support test, unlike tweezers, which compare lows.
Opposite-color marubozu candles separated by a full-range gap. Conventional direction follows the second candle.
Same kicking geometry, but direction follows the longer marubozu. A direction-policy variant, not independent evidence of a second occurrence.
Opposite-color candles open near the same price; second is a long belt-hold candle. Continuation direction follows the second body, with matching prior trend required.
Long down candle; next up candle opens below its low and closes near that low. Bearish continuation context.
Long down candle; next up candle opens below its low and closes just inside the prior body, near the prior close. Bearish continuation context.
Long down candle; next up candle opens below its low and recovers into the body, beyond the near-close area but below its midpoint. Bearish continuation context.
Long down body, small downward body-gapped star, then an up candle penetrating the first body. Bullish; save penetration threshold.
Long up body, small upward body-gapped star, then a down candle penetrating the first body. Bearish.
Morning-star structure with a doji as the middle candle. More specific subtype; avoid duplicate recommendations.
Evening-star structure with a middle doji. Same subtype relationship.
Middle doji isolated by full-range gaps on both sides; third body reverses into the first. Stricter than a doji star.
Three up candles with progressively higher closes, opens within/near prior bodies and short upper shadows, subject to body-size checks. Bullish-context study.
Three descending down candles, opening inside preceding down bodies and closing near lows. The reference detector also checks a preceding up candle, so its input pattern uses four bars.
Three descending down candles with short lower shadows, each later open near the preceding close. More specific bearish form.
Harami pair followed by an opposite-to-first candle closing beyond the first open. The third candle already supplies confirmation.
Engulfing pair followed by a further close in the engulfing direction. Preserve parent-pair relationship and later confirmation time.
Up candle, upward body-gapped down candle, then another down candle opening inside the second body and closing within the first up body. Three candles despite the name.
Long up body, gapped small down body, then a down body engulfing the second but still closing above the first close. Distinct from two crows.
Three higher-closing up candles whose bodies/shadows show a weakening advance. Bearish warning setup; do not assume every occurrence reverses.
Three higher-closing up candles; the last is a small body near the top of the preceding long candle. Bearish-context setup.
Three down candles with shrinking bodies/ranges: a long lower-shadow first candle, smaller second, then a small contained marubozu. Bullish-context study; use exact reference low relationships.
Long down candle, down harami body making a lower low, then a small up candle in the lower area. Bullish traditional interpretation; confirmation tested separately.
Three doji; the middle body gaps away and the third retreats toward the opposite side. Direction depends on whether the middle is the upper or lower star.
Down/up/down sequence with approximately equal first and third closes and the middle candle trading above that level. Bullish-context support pattern.
Two similar up bodies with nearby opens both stand across a body gap from the first candle. Direction follows gap direction, even when the later candles are up.
Body gap in one direction, then an opposite-color candle opening within the preceding body and retreating into—but not filling—the gap. Continuation context.
Three candles: two same-color bodies separated by a gap, then an opposite candle that fills the gap. Distinct from Tasuki's unfilled gap.

Three advancing/declining same-color candles followed by a large opposite candle spanning their move. Reference sign follows the first three candles' continuation direction. Any opposite reversal interpretation must be a separate research variant.
Five candles: long directional body, three smaller opposing candles constrained by reference range checks, then a long candle resuming the original direction.

Five candles: long up candle, upward-gapped small reaction, two further shallow reaction candles, then an up candle above reaction highs. The library detects bullish only; bearish mirror would be custom.
Five candles: long body, same-direction body gap and extension, then an opposite final candle returning into the original gap.
Five candles: three declining down candles, a fourth down candle with an upper shadow, then an up candle opening above the fourth open and closing above its high.
Four down candles: two marubozu, a gapped-down third whose upper shadow reaches the prior body, and a fourth engulfing the third's full range. Bullish traditional interpretation.
Inside bar followed by a directional range displacement; a reversal through the inside-bar boundary within three bars confirms the trap. Preserve setup versus confirmed library outputs.
Adds a preceding nested-range condition and a close near an extreme before the ordinary trap displacement. Four-bar setup, optional subsequent confirmation within three bars.
Two adjacent bars test highs/lows within max(one known tick, 0.1 prior ATR); second closes away from the tested level. Require preceding advance/decline.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Confirm through the pair's opposite extreme. Distinct from matching closes.

entries.name_and_variants: Inside bar; single / nested / mother-bar cluster
entries.definition: Entire second range lies within the first, with at least one strict edge. Nested ranges and multiple inside bars share the original mother-bar identity.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Close beyond mother-bar high/low. Body-only containment is harami, not this pattern.

entries.definition: Second high exceeds first high and second low falls below first low. Tag close in the top/bottom quarter of the second range.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Study next-open entry or later range break separately; distinct from body engulfing.

entries.name_and_variants: Pin bar / rejection bar; upper/lower shadow
entries.definition: Dominant shadow at least twice the body and 60% of total range; opposite shadow at most 15% of range. Exclude zero range; use prior trend as metadata.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Close beyond the short-shadow end. Overlaps hammer/shooting-star families; link shared event.

entries.definition: Current range is strictly smallest among the most recent four/seven complete candles. Inside-NR also satisfies PA02. Equal minima are a separate optional tie variant.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Break above/below the contraction range; direction is unknown at detection.

entries.definition: An inside-bar cluster is followed by a breach of a mother-bar edge, then a close back inside within three bars.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Confirm through the opposite edge later; retain failure and confirmation times. Hikkake overlap is annotated, not assumed equivalent.

entries.definition: Current low exceeds prior high, or current high is below prior low. Require both adjacent intervals to be complete; no fabricated bars.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Gap-hold, gap-fill and retest are separate outcome/strategy variants.

entries.definition: Open beyond the previous full range, then close back inside that range on the same completed candle. Bullish closes in the upper half, bearish in the lower half.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Entry can only follow that close. Distinguish an opening gap reversal from an island requiring two full gaps.

entries.definition: Two similarly sized directional legs AB and CD separated by the BC correction; completion is at D.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; price equality and time symmetry recorded separately.

entries.definition: CD extends the AB-sized projection rather than matching it; distinguish the 1.27 and 1.618 extensions.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; separate extension IDs.

entries.definition: B near the 0.618 retracement of XA and D near the 0.786 retracement, with supporting AB=CD/BC alignment.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; retracement structure stays inside X.

entries.definition: B shallower than 0.618 of XA; D near 0.886; stronger BC extension distinguishes it from Gartley.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; 0.382/0.50 B-point subtypes.

entries.definition: Shallower B-point structure with terminal extension near 1.13 of XA rather than the standard Bat retracement.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; distinct from an invalid standard Bat.

entries.definition: B near 0.786 of XA; D extends past X, with the ideal 1.27 XA projection and supporting leg relationships.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; wider extensions need separately specified variants.

entries.definition: Terminal 1.618 XA extension, with a shallower B retracement and an extreme BC projection.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; keep distinct from Deep Crab.

entries.definition: Shares the 1.618 XA terminal extension but B lies near 0.886 of XA.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; deeper B is the distinguishing constraint.

entries.definition: Extended impulse returns toward the initial support/resistance region, combining a 0.886–1.13 OX retracement/extension zone with an extreme impulse relationship.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; use O-X-A-B-C notation rather than silently borrowing Gartley labels.

entries.definition: Strong BC reversal leg of 1.618–2.24 times AB, followed by a D retracement near half of BC, with reciprocal AB=CD alignment.
entries.coverage_or_priority: Bull/bear; a first-pullback structure rather than an ordinary M/W.
